messages:
inc-bot: ALERT: Auto-pager triggered -> high OOM rate on decode-pool-9. Symptoms: CUDA OOM during streaming decode, node flaps. Paging @jordan (sre) and ops oncall.

jordan (sre): I'm seeing repeated OOMs on decode-rt-9-{0..3} starting ~6137891200. Spike in decoding token growth. Likely runaway generation. Dumping logs now.

alex (infra): Confirmed node restarts 3x in last 4m. Kube reports container OOMKilled. No host kernel OOM.

jordan (sre): log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T03:14:02Z] cuda: out of memory when allocating 123456789 bytes
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/serve/decode.py\", line 742, in stream_step
    out = model.forward_step(...)
  File \"/opt/runtime/decoder.cu\", line 112, in decode
    raise CUDARuntimeError('OOM')
```

maya (runtime): Also seeing massive KV cache growth for sessions with no max_tokens set. Router is passing client header `X-Client-Max-Tokens: null` for some requests (bad SDK edge case).

ops (oncall): Quick question — any customer reports?

sam (support): Two customers flagged increased 502s and partial responses (support ticket #C-17421 and #C-17422). I'll open an incident status with them and advise degraded throughput.

jordan (sre): Immediate mitigations proposal: 1) throttle request rate for decode-pool-9 (limit concurrent decodes) 2) evict long-running streams > 30s 3) enable fallback to quantized-cpu-decoder for overflow requests 4) sanitize header to enforce hard max_tokens <= 2048 at router.

alex (infra): I'm going to cordon decode-rt-9-2 and drain pods gracefully to stop flapping node. Will apply concurrency limit via gateway rule now.

deploy-bot: rolling update started for route `decode.v1` -> applying runtime-config:concurrency=80,stream-timeout=30s.

maya (runtime): Patch ready for router header sanitation. Pushing hotfix to staging then prod. It drops null/max header and forces `max_generation_tokens=512` if missing.

jordan (sre): Oncall, please run `kubectl exec -n inference router-xx -- curl -X POST http://localhost/config -d '{"max_tokens_policy":"enforce"}'` to toggle enforcement, or I'll run it if you approve.

ops (oncall): Approved. Running now.

ops (oncall): Done. Enforcement toggled. Monitoring telemetry.

jordan (sre): Early telemetry: OOM events per minute down from 9 -> 1 in decode-pool-9, request drops still present but decreasing. We evicted ~120 long-running streams.

sam (support): Customer update: sent initial notice citing degraded performance and ongoing mitigation. They ask for ETA to full recovery.

maya (runtime): Suggest we enable fallback path for tokens > 512 to quantized model to avoid further GPU pressure; that will slightly increase latency but avoid OOM.

alex (infra): Fallback toggle done via feature-flag: `ff-enable-quant-fallthrough=on`. Applied to decode-pool-9.

jordan (sre): Metrics: 6137891240 -> 6137891260 window: 1) OOMs decreased 78% 2) dropped requests ~1.2k total during incident window 3) customer visible 502s from two customers resolved after evictions/fallback.

sam (support): Notified customers with summary + mitigation. They'll be monitoring logs.

jordan (sre): Root cause hypothesis: SDK edge case sending null/oversized max_tokens allowed runaway generation; router didn't sanitize header. We'll publish a post-incident with fix + SDK patch.

maya (runtime): Follow-ups: ship router header sanitizer, add unit test for null header, add telemetry alert on KV cache per-session growth, and set default hard cap in serving runtime of 2048 tokens to avoid silent runaway.

jordan (sre): Handoff: I'm handing to @maya for follow-up and postmortem. Oncall remains ops. If regressions occur, re-open pager.

ops (oncall): Acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring for 2h.

jordan (sre): Closing thread for now — will add incident doc + customer impact numbers to postmortem. :white_check_mark:
